action: Malwarebytes advises checking shortened links before clicking, even when the post comes from a trusted brand. General advice: spot-check your own old Bitly links and replace any that no longer lead to the right page.
exec: Short links in old posts, emails or print can be repointed after they go inactive; organisations relying on them should check where they lead.
plain: Old Bitly short links in years-old X posts by public figures and companies were redirected to unrelated pages. Bitly says bad actors reused old, inactive links and it is disabling them.
summary: CNN, via KSL, reports that this weekend some old Bitly short links in X posts, seemingly confined to 2009 to 2014, by politicians, agencies and companies, were redirected to unrelated content. Bitly said on X it identified an issue that let bad actors repurpose old, inactive links, suspended the accounts involved and is disabling the affected URLs. Malwarebytes reports a hijacked link in a 2011 McDonald's post now leads to an error page.
title: Bitly short links hijacked

validation.note: Two independent publishers: CNN (relayed by KSL) and Malwarebytes (16 Nov, citing Cybernews) both report the redirected links and Bitly's statement that it suspended the accounts involved and is disabling the links; Bitly's own X post was not read. KonBriefing tracker entry dropped.

review.note: Action advice unsourced (now Malwarebytes / General advice); '2009 to 2014' qualified as seemingly confined per KSL; Bitly statement and McDonald's example match
